intent: Repair the deterministic generic NATS redelivery failure in which an omitted A2A context_id is regenerated differently on each delivery and conflicts with immutable execution identity. Derive one opaque stable 12-hex server context from exact durable wire identity and task coordinates before the first spine/server identity write, preserve explicit contexts, and retain fail-closed behavior for foreign identity or context drift.

negative_controls.name: redelivery-and-context-negatives
negative_controls.command: /Users/dhyana/dharma_swarm/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/test_nats_transport.py -k 'redelivery or context_id or immutable_context'

commit.message: fix(a2a): stabilize missing NATS redelivery context

interface_mismatches: NATS wire tasks may legitimately omit context_id, but each redelivery currently receives a fresh random server context.
ExecutionIdentity correctly treats context_id as immutable once observed, so a second delivery fails before its handler can retry.
The governed Mission Control A2A path already supplies a stable context; the generic transport must provide equivalent stability without weakening identity immutability.
honest_blockers: A deterministic context prevents identity drift but does not itself prove broker liveness, handler usefulness, or semantic acceptance.
Explicit client-supplied context remains authoritative and must never be silently rewritten.
A context collision or foreign execution identity must continue to fail closed.
session_entry.rollback: Revert the deterministic missing-context derivation, its regression controls, and this packet. Existing explicit-context dispatch remains unchanged; generic missing-context redelivery returns to the known fail-closed but non-retriable baseline.
